The owner authorized recovery of the stuck Bluetooth service. The launch-control restart was refused by macOS protection, a normal termination signal did not stop the old process, and an authorized forced termination let macOS relaunch the same service. The replacement process is idle in the final observation. No browser tabs were closed by the agent. Browser access to Chrome's internal suspension page was refused by the tool's URL policy. Memory headroom later recovered through normal system/user activity; this record does not attribute that recovery to a specific action.

Two complete three-pair comparisons at separate 14 and 22 GB ceilings were frozen before any new performance output. The first 14 GB attempt was interrupted after CPU contention made its timings unusable. The second attempt was also timing-excluded and stopped before another model launch when thermal state was non-nominal. Their complete files remain here. No speed outcome was inspected to select a candidate, change a native recipe or choose a favorable subset.

The existing runner then gained a separate prospective pilot-only policy. It records one-second CPU snapshots, excludes any known build/storage job and competing CPU observed consecutively for at least five seconds, and retains shorter spikes as diagnostics. It requires twenty continuously quiet nominal seconds before each process, with a five-minute waiting ceiling. These are explicit operating heuristics intended to distinguish desktop repaint bursts from sustained load, not proof that shorter activity has no effect. The current evidence is the transient renderer exclusions and successful policy/child-process fixtures. There is no runtime knob that silently changes this frozen policy. Revisit it through another prospective protocol if observed variance or operating conditions show it insufficient. The historical immediate-exclusion policy and old verdicts remain unchanged. Thermal, power, paging, physical-process, headroom, pressure and storage gates remain in force.

All twenty runner tests pass. The new full comparison retains the original 14/22 GB targets, three paired rounds, workloads, two pack recipes and frozen native binary. Its protocol digest is e0ff7285164adabfb48c280623003becef5a80ec46fac5564018bd741de6db36. All twelve processes and their natural-answer completion checks finish inside their physical budgets. Five cells are timing-excluded because of sustained background CPU or paging. The frozen analyzer therefore produces no clean medians or speed qualification; seven individually eligible cells are not selected into a replacement result. The timing comparison is discarded, while functional/process-memory observations remain valid within their stated scope. No alternate pack is promoted, published or admitted to Auto.

The executable is still the frozen practical-v11 build previously captured in [[sources/runs/2026/10/2026-10-05-native-practical-comparison-prepared]]. The files below preserve all new policies, tests, attempts, supervision, native receipts and analysis. Each block is zlib-compressed exact bytes encoded as base64, with its original size and SHA-256. No model weights or binary payloads are embedded.
